Subject: Significant spikes in first-token latency (p95/p99) since Friday

Hi Jordan —

We started seeing large regressions in first-token latency for requests through the Hosted API starting Friday night (UTC). p95 has moved from ~120ms to ~420–550ms and p99 is reporting bursts up to ~1.2s for a subset of requests. This is impacting our response times for interactive workflows (search & assistant flows).

Attached are traces and a short capture from our synthetic monitors showing the increase in time-to-first-token (TTFT). We also included a few request IDs that reproduce the spike. The pattern looks like an extra handshake/round-trip is happening before the first byte.

We need this escalated — this is customer-impacting and our execs are asking for immediate mitigation and a timeline. Can you confirm you've opened an internal incident and share next steps?

Attachments: alcyon_latency_traces.zip (zip, 2.4 MB)

Thanks,

Quick triage notes (10:20 PT):

What we see:
- Customer traces show consistent extra ~200–600ms on initial TLS handshake for requests routed via a subset of CDN POPs in the western US.
- Internal telemetry shows an increased rate of TLS handshake renegotiation and failed session resumption for the same time windows.
- Error rate (5xx) not materially elevated; this looks like a latency/regression rather than request failures.

Hypothesis: Something changed in the vendor CDN-to-upstream handoff (SNI routing or TLS params) causing additional round-trips for the initial TLS handshake. Could be session resumption falling back and causing a full handshake.

Attachments: initial-triage-notes.txt

Next steps:
- Rishi/Sean to pull tcpdump/TLS debug logs for the customer request IDs (Rishi: syslogs point to dropped TCP retransmits between CDN edge and our egress in some cases).
- If confirmed, propose temporary route bypass to avoid affected POPs while we work with the CDN vendor.
- Jordan/Marissa: start preparing a concise customer update with mitigation options and timeline.

Subject: RE: Significant spikes in first-token latency (p95/p99) since Friday — infra findings

Team — brief infra analysis from the first-pass investigation:

Observations:
- Reproduced elevated TTFT by replaying request IDs from the traces (see example timings below). curl --trace-time shows an extra 180–350ms before TLS handshake completes for affected flows.
- TLS debug shows full full-handshake events where we would expect session resumption. Session ticket/ID not being honored by the CDN edge for ~12% of connections in the affected window.
- Packet captures indicate additional SYN/ACK retransmits and occasional out-of-order ACKs on the path between the CDN POP and our cloud egress (ASNs X and Y). The retransmit spikes line up with the times Kate provided.

Example (trimmed):
- curl -w "%{time_starttransfer} %{time_total}" -I https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> 0.48s 0.95s (affected)
- baseline (non-affected POP): 0.12s 0.28s

Likely root cause (working hypothesis):
- Vendor CDN is failing to reuse TLS sessions on some handoff paths, forcing full handshakes; combined with increased packet loss/retransmits on the CDN->egress path this adds an extra RTT to TTFT.

Immediate mitigations proposed (ACTIONABLE):
1) Bypass affected CDN POPs for Alcyon traffic by adding a route rule for their ingress ASN at the edge (low-risk, reversible) — estimated customer-impact window: minutes to implement, validated within 15–30 minutes.
2) Ask CDN vendor to enable stricter session resumption or investigate SNI routing anomalies (longer term).
3) Enable HTTP/3 (QUIC) on the affected prefix to reduce handshake RTTs where supported (pilot).

Risks: route bypass will increase egress cost slightly for that traffic; session changes require vendor coordination and may need cert chain checks.

If you approve, I can enact the bypass now and we can monitor TTFT for Alcyon.

—Rishi

Subject: Redwood update: mitigation plan and next steps (TTFT surge)

Kate —

Thanks again for raising this and for the traces — they've been invaluable. Short executive summary and what we did between Mon–Thu: 

What happened:
- Starting late Friday, a subset of requests routed through a small number of CDN POPs experienced a change in TLS session behavior combined with intermittent packet retransmits on the CDN->our egress path. That combination led to an extra full TLS handshake and an added RTT, producing the observed p95/p99 TTFT spikes.

What we did (mitigation executed at 11:10 PT Tue):
- Implemented an immediate route bypass for Alcyon traffic away from the affected CDN POPs (Rishi). Observed customer TTFT p95 drop from ~480ms to ~140ms within 20 minutes of the change.
- Opened a ticket with the CDN vendor to investigate session resumption and SNI routing anomalies (assigned to their engineering team).
- Started a pilot to enable HTTP/3 for Alcyon egress where supported (reduces handshake RTTs).

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency returned to acceptable levels post-bypass. We will continue to monitor P95/P99 for the next 72 hours and provide daily updates.

Compensation/next steps:
- We're prepared to offer a one-time service credit for the customer impact window and will surface suggested credit amount via the account team.
- Propose a 30-minute postmortem call on Monday (Jul 27) to review root cause and a permanent remediation plan.

Attachments: redwood_sla_summary.pdf

Please let us know if you'd like any immediate adjustments to the mitigation or if you'd prefer we keep traffic on the bypass while the vendor remediates. Happy to jump on a call with your leadership.

Best,
